newsitem.title: THAILAND: Banker Thanong chosen new Thai finance minister.
newsitem.headline: Banker Thanong chosen new Thai finance minister.

text.p: Thanong Bidaya, a little-known banker, was appointed Thailand's new finance minister on Friday to succeed the well-respected Amnuay Viravan, who quit over policy differences with rivals in the government.

"His appointment has already received the assent from King Bhumibol Adulyadej and he will assume office after his swearing in depending on the King's convenience," said Poosana Premanoch, deputy secretary general to the Thai prime minister.
Thanong, 50, is president of the Thai Military Bank Plc. He is expected to hold a news conference late on Friday night.

Thanong will replace Amnuay, who resigned on Thursday over policy differences with political rivals in Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh's six-party coalition government over his management of Thailand' ailing economy.
The new minister is said by government officials to be close to Chavalit, officials in the premier's office said.
Political sources said Thanong was chosen after several other economic heavyweights had turned down the job offered to them by Chavalit.

The Thai government is grappling with steps to draw the country out of its worst economic crisis in over a decade and is in dire need of a strong economic leader to put the economy back on an even keel, analysts said.
Thanong will be Thailand's sixth finance minister since 1995 under three governments.
Analysts said Thanong's image was less illustrious than the respected Amnuay, who has had a high-profile 30-year public career as civil servant, banker, politician and minister.
But the Thai stock market, which sank this week to eight-year-lows on Amnuay's resignation, rallied partly on the news of Thanong's appointment, brokers said.
The index finished up 15.48 points, or 3.33 percent, higher at 480.25, after closing down for the past eight days.
Brokers said the quick move by the government to fill in an important portfolio during the period of economic crisis and a technical rebound helped the market rise.
